passage:
Instead of burying a metal box, Class 812 made a digital time capsule. Each student recorded a short video message to their future self.
They talked about favorite songs, worries, dreams, and what they thought the world would be like in ten years. The videos were saved on several devices and given to the school archive.
One student asked, "What if the file cannot open in the future?"
The teacher said that was a real problem. Digital memories need care too. Formats change, devices break, and passwords are forgotten.
The project taught students that saving the future is not only about what to store. It is also about how to keep it readable.
